newsitem.title: FRANCE: GM sees 15.5 mln U.S. car sales in '97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: GM sees 15.5 mln U.S. car sales in '97 - paper.

text.p: General Motors Corp chairman Jack Smith confirmed in an interview on Monday that the U.S. carmaker expects U.S. car sales this year to reach 15.5 million units and forecast they would exceed 15 million units again next year.

"The U.S. car market will be better than anticipated. We expect to end the year with 15.5 million (sales). 1997 should also be a good year, (with sales) above 15 million," Smith told the French newspaper La Tribune.
In the first eight months of the year, Smith said GM's car sales had risen two percent in western Europe, 67 percent in eastern Europe and 1.3 percent in the Asia-Pacific region.
"GM may sell 75,000 vehicles in Japan this year, of which 43,000 would be Opels. These models are better for the Japanese market," he said.

"Toyota is making a real effort to sell our Cavalier in accordance with our agreements. We'll sell fewer this year than the 20,000 expected. But we won't be far off. We're introducing right-hand drive models," he said.
GM plans to launch the Saturn in Japan next year.
"We expect to exceed 100,000 sales there by the year 2000," he said.
